\section{Static Expressions}
\seclabel{static-expr}

\note{Static expressions are not yet supported.}

\emph{Static expressions} denote \emph{static values}.  Conceptually,
a static expression is not evaluated while a program is running, and
thus its evaluation
cannot complete abruptly.  Given instantiations of all static
parameters (described in \chapref{trait-parameters}) in scope of a
static expression, the value of the static expression can be
determined statically.  Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as
\emph{static arguments} which instantiate static parameters and
\KWD{where}-clause constraints (described in \secref{where-clauses}).
We define the set of static
expressions by first defining the types of static expressions, and
distinguishing static values from the closely related literal values.
We then describe the expressions that evaluate to the various kinds of
static values.


\subsection{Types of Static Expressions}

There are three groups of traits that describe literals
and static expressions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The \emph{literal} traits, which describe boolean,
  character, string, and numerals.  For example, the literal \VAR{true} has
  trait \EXP{\TYP{BooleanLiteral}\llbracket\VAR{true}\rrbracket} and a
  character literal has trait \TYP{Character}.
See \secref{literals} for a discussion of Fortress literals.

\item The \emph{constant} traits, which describe values denoted by
expressions composed from literals and operators (described in
\secref{constant-values});
the type of a constant expression encodes the value of the expression.
For example, the type of a constant expression \EXP{3+5},
%IntegerConstant[\false, 3+5\]
\EXP{\TYP{IntegerConstant}\llbracket\VAR{false}, 3+5\rrbracket},
encodes the value of the expression; the operator \EXP{+} is
used in the static arguments.  When an operator is not supported in static
arguments, \library\ can still encode the value of the expression by
providing a specific constant trait such as
\EXP{\TYP{RationalValueTimesPi}\llbracket\VAR{false},1,1\rrbracket}
(described in \secref{pi}).



\item The \emph{static} traits, which describe values denoted by
expressions composed from literals, operators (described in
\secref{constant-values}), and \KWD{bool}, \KWD{nat},
and \KWD{int} parameters; here the type
does not encode the value of the expression, but the value of the
expression can nevertheless be known statically if specific
values are specified for the static parameters.  Also, in situations
where the type of an expression composed solely from literals and
operators nevertheless cannot be described by a constant trait, then a
static trait may be used to describe it instead.
For example, a static expression \EXP{2(3+m)} where \VAR{m} is a
\KWD{nat} parameter has trait \TYP{NaturalStatic}.
\end{enumerate}


The only operation on literals that produces a new literal (as opposed
to a constant) is concatenation by using the operator \EXP{\|}.
One may concatenate mixed string and
character literals, producing a string literal.
For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
One may also concatenate two natural numerals

content.content:
rule to accept a pair of overloaded functional declarations.  If a
pair of overloaded declarations satisfies any one of the three rules,
it is considered a valid overloading.

The overloading rules given in this chapter are disjoint.  That is, at
most one rule applies to each pair of overloaded declarations.  It is
possible for new rules to be added which allow additional
overloadings.

\label{adv-over-kwd}
Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical
(up to $\alpha$-equivalence).  Also, valid overloadings for
declarations that contain keyword or
varargs parameters are determined
by analyzing the expansion of these declarations as described in
\secref{applicability-with-special-params}.  Therefore, static
parameters, keyword parameters,
and varargs parameters are ignored in
the remainder of this chapter.

An operator method declaration whose name is one of the operator parameters
(described in \secref{opr-ident})
of its enclosing trait or object may be overloaded with other operator
declarations in the same component.  Therefore, such an operator method
declaration must satisfy the overloading rules
with every operator declaration in the same component.



In addition, a functional which takes a single parameter of type
a naked type parameter of bound \TYP{Any} cannot be
overloaded.  This restriction prevents ambiguous overloadings such as
the following:
%makeSet[\T extends Any\](x: T): Set[\T\]
%makeSet[\T extends Any\](x: T, y: T): Set[\T\]
\begin{Fortress}
\(\VAR{makeSet}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends}\mskip 4mu plus 4mu\TYP{Any}\rrbracket(x\COLON T)\COLON \TYP{Set}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)\\
\(\VAR{makeSet}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends}\mskip 4mu plus 4mu\TYP{Any}\rrbracket(x\COLON T, y\COLON T)\COLON \TYP{Set}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)
\end{Fortress}
The type parameter of \EXP{\VAR{makeSet}} may be instantiated with
\TYP{(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Z})} or \TYP{\mathbb{Z}}.  If this is the
case then the call \EXP{\VAR{makeSet}(3, 4)}, where 3 and 4 have type
\TYP{\mathbb{Z}}, is ambiguous.

\secref{subtype-rule} states the \emph{Subtype Rule}, which stipulates
that the parameter type of one declaration be a subtype of the
parameter type of the other.  In this case, there is no possibility of
ambiguous calls, because one declaration is more specific than the
other.  This section also places a restriction on the return types of
the overloaded declarations to ensure that type safety is not
violated.  \secref{incompatibility-rule} defines the \emph{
Incompatibility Rule} that, if satisfied by a pair of declarations,
guarantees that neither declaration is applicable to the same
functional call.  In \secref{more-specific-rule}, the \emph{Meet Rule}
requires the existence of a declaration that is more specific than
both overloaded declarations in the situation that both are applicable
to a given call.

In the remainder of this chapter, we build on the terminology and
notation defined in \chapref{multiple-dispatch}
and \chapref{conversions-coercions}.



\section{Subtype Rule}
\seclabel{subtype-rule}

If the parameter type of one declaration is a subtype of the parameter
type of another (and they are not the same) then there is no
ambiguity between these two declarations: for every call to which both
are applicable, the first is more specific.  This is the basis of the
Subtype Rule.

The Subtype Rule also requires a relationship between the return types
of the two declarations.  Without such a requirement, a program may
violate type safety.

\paragraph{The Subtype Rule for Functions and Functional Methods:}
Suppose that $\f(\Ps) : \Us$ and $\f(\Qs) : \Vs$ are two distinct
function or functional method declarations in a single scope.
If $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$ and $\Us \Ovrsubtype \Vs$ then $\f(\Ps)$ and
$\f(\Qs)$ are a valid overloading.

\paragraph{The Subtype Rule for Dotted Methods:}

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

\begin{theorem}
Let $d_1 = \hdeclg{f}{\Delta_1}{S_1}{T_1}$ and $d_2 = \hdeclg{f}{\Delta_2}{S_2}{T_2}$ be declarations

the arrow type $\sigma_{\wedge} = \forall\ob{\Delta_1, \Delta_2}(S_1 \cap S_2) \rightarrow T_2$.

#!/bin/bash
# Every command of the nat-shadow followup, in order.  Run from $FORTRESS_HOME:
#
#   ./explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/run-all.sh <work-dir>
#
# <work-dir> is a scratch directory OUTSIDE the repository.  Nothing tracked is
# modified; default_repository/ is never written (every run gets its own
# -Dfortress.caches / FORTRESS_CACHES).  The shadow is rebuilt from
# ../shadow.patch exactly as ../run-all.sh does it -- the patch now carries the
# two followup fixes, so no separate step is needed.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.."                     # $FORTRESS_HOME
source explorations/experiment/env.sh
D=explorations/perf-probes/nat
F=$D/followup
P=explorations/perf-probes/prelude
DC=$P/desugar-codegen
W=${1:?usage: run-all.sh <work-dir>}
mkdir -p "$W"
CP=$(./bin/fortress_classpath 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
NAT=$D/shadow-classes
newcache () { local c=$1; rm -rf "$c"; mkdir -p "$c"; printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$c/global.map"; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------ the shadow
SHADOWED="scala_src/typechecker/Formula.scala scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala
          scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala
          scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala
          scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala
          scala_src/typechecker/AbstractMethodChecker.scala"
if [ ! -d $D/shadow-src ]; then
  for rel in $SHADOWED; do
    mkdir -p "$(dirname $D/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/$rel)"
    cp ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/$rel $D/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/$rel
  done
  patch -p7 -d $D/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress --forward < $D/shadow.patch
  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain ProjectFortress/src)" ]; then
    echo "ABORT: the patch touched tracked sources" >&2; exit 1; fi
fi
rm -rf $NAT; mkdir -p $NAT
java -Xmx2g -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -d $NAT -classpath "$CP" -encoding UTF-8 \
grep -v '^@@PROBE    at \|^	at ' $W/g-lib.out > $W/g-lib.clean
norm () { sed 's#'"$PWD"'/##g' "$1" | grep -v '^ELAPSED\|^# start\|^# classpath\|^##########'; }
{ echo "# Left = nat shadow + BOTH followup fixes; Right = the committed captures."
  diff -u <(norm $W/g-lib.clean) <(norm $D/03a-lib-worldflip-after.out)
  echo; diff -u <(norm $W/g-lib.clean) <(norm $D/03c-lib-argsalwaysequal.out) && echo "(identical)"
} > $F/f5-lib-diff.txt 2>&1

# --- 4. the per-declaration run, which now finishes; and the timing A/B
$DC/make-shadows.sh "$W/dc-src" "$W/dc-classes"
javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$W/dc-classes" $DC/PhaseProbe.java
perdecl () { local c=$W/c-$1; newcache "$c"
  { echo "########## PhaseProbe -order typecheck Library/FortressLibrary.fss (tolerant, per declaration)"
    echo "# classpath prefix: $2 ${4:-}"; S=$(date +%s)
    timeout ${3:-2400} java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow ${4:-} \
         -Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dfortress.caches="$c" -cp "$2$W/dc-classes:$CP" \
         PhaseProbe -order typecheck Library/FortressLibrary.fss
    echo "exit=$?"; echo "ELAPSED $(( $(date +%s) - S )) s"; } > "$W/$1" 2>&1; }
# the timing A/B: 180 s each, counting declarations reached
perdecl t-stock.out   ""      180
perdecl t-memo.out    "$NAT:" 180
perdecl t-nomemo.out  "$NAT:" 180 -Dprobe.nat.noParentsMemo=true
for f in t-stock.out t-memo.out t-nomemo.out; do
  echo "$f: decls=$(grep -c '@@TC DECL-' $W/$f)"; done
# and the whole run, with the error texts
perdecl h-perdecl-final.out "$NAT:" 2400
perdecl h-perdecl-errors.out "$NAT:" 2400 -Dprobe.dumpErrors=true
#!/bin/bash
# Generate and compile the probe's shadow classes.  See shadow-patch.py.
# usage: make-shadows.sh <shadow-src-dir> <shadow-classes-dir>
set -eu
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$HERE/../../../.."                     # $FORTRESS_HOME
SHADOW_SRC=$1
SHADOW_OUT=$2
mkdir -p "$SHADOW_SRC" "$SHADOW_OUT"
python3 "$HERE/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SHADOW_SRC"
CP=$(./bin/fortress_classpath 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SHADOW_OUT" \
      "$SHADOW_SRC/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
      "$SHADOW_SRC/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
      "$SHADOW_SRC/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
      "$SHADOW_SRC/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
      "$SHADOW_SRC/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java"
echo "shadow classes in $SHADOW_OUT"

<target name="compileAll" depends="compileCommon, makeAST, parser, operatorsGen"
          description="Compile all Fortress code.">
    <!-- Joint Java+Scala compilation, formerly the <scalac> Ant task
         (removed from Scala 2.13): the .java sources are passed to scalac
         too, which parses them for signatures but emits classes only for
         the .scala sources; the javac step below then compiles the .java
         sources for real.  The file list goes through an @argfile to keep
         the command line short. -->
    <pathconvert property="scalac.compileAll.sources" pathsep="${line.separator}">
      <fileset dir="${src}">
        <include name="**/*.java"/>
        <include name="**/*.scala"/>
        <exclude name="${usefulPackage}/*.java"/>
        <exclude name="${unicodePackage}/*.java"/>
      </fileset>
    </pathconvert>
    <pathconvert property="scalac.compileAll.classpath" refid="compile.classpath"/>
    <echo file="${build}/scalac-compileAll.args" message="${scalac.compileAll.sources}"/>
    <java classname="scala.tools.nsc.Main" fork="true" failonerror="true"
          maxmemory="1024m">
      <classpath refid="scala.classpath"/>
      <arg value="-d"/>
      <arg value="${build}"/>
      <arg value="-classpath"/>
      <arg value="${scalac.compileAll.classpath}"/>
      <arg value="-encoding"/>
      <arg value="UTF-8"/>
      <arg value="-deprecation"/>
      <arg value="@${build}/scalac-compileAll.args"/>

    <javac encoding="UTF-8"

      <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>

# Collaboration protocol

How Pavol and Claude work together on the Fortress revival. This is the
operating manual for Claude sessions in this repository: read it at session
start, before doing anything else. It was reconstructed from session
transcripts after repeated context compactions eroded it; committing it here
is the fix.

Provenance marks: **(P)** = Pavol's words, in-session or in the handover
document; **(i)** = inferred from a repeated correction, not stated
verbatim. Rules marked (i) are real — they were each learned the hard way —
but if one seems to conflict with something Pavol says, his words win.

## 1. Roles

- **(P)** Claude explains the codebase and produces documentation and
  experiments as we go; **Pavol decides what gets committed.**
- **(P)** When in doubt, ask before acting. Surface discrepancies and diffs
  to Pavol; do not resolve them silently.
- **(P)** Standing approval exists for exactly two things: *"I approve the
  above modernization plan. Continue autonomously. Delegate to workers where
  it makes sense."* — scoped to the approved ladder in
  `modernization-plan.md`, not a general license — and the `main`
  fast-forward standing order in §4.
- **(P)** Use idle time — "there's no need for you to idle with empty
  hands." While waiting on builds or feedback, advance parked research or
  documentation.
- **(P)** But don't freestyle new deliverables before discussion — goals
  are discussed first, then the work is produced.

The compiled type checker now checks `nat` and `int` static parameters, a size such as the `n` of `Vector[\RR64, n\]`, by the plan's minimal design: a size is a symbol or a literal, two sizes are equal when they are the same symbol or the same literal, an inference variable is bound by equality, and there is no arithmetic. ## 2. Where the fix belongs

The map's row for `nat` and `int` parameters puts the wall in the checker: `STypesUtil.scala:550-557`, "interp works / comp absent — the wall is the checker, not codegen" (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:233`, and `:355` in the path table). The checker is the TYPECHECK phase of the compiler's order, `compiler/StaticChecker.java` calling the Scala checker (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:266`, `:353`). Code generation already names a size (`NamingCzar.forIntRef`/`forIntBase`, `explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:36-38`) and fails later at load, which is the run-time rung's (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:93`). So the fix is in `scala_src/`, and in the one Java class the checker calls on every method invocation, `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` (reached from `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:606` and `:730`). Nothing in `compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `runtimeSystem/`, `compiler/runtimeValues/`, `CodeGen.java` or `OverloadSet.java` was edited.

## 3. Precedent search

- **Inference variables.** The checker has two, both syntax-tree nodes minted with `new Object()` identity: `_InferenceVarType` (`Fortress.ast:1061`, `NodeFactory.java:1166-1175`) and `_InferenceVarOp` (`Fortress.ast:1593`, `NodeFactory.java:1178-1180`). No inference variable in the tree is a reserved name. The size variable follows them (decision 1 below).
- **Equality-only constraints.** The operator track is the one whose constraints are equalities only (`OPrimitive(pe, ne)`, `Formula.scala:57-61`): its reduce steps `oSimplify`, `oContradiction`, `oTrivial` (`:355-371`), its cliques (`getCliques`, `makeSub`, `:640-642`), its primitive constructors (`:802-806`) and `TypeAnalyzer.pEqv(Op, Op)` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:342-348`). The size track copies each of these once, with `nEq` in place of `==`. The interpreter's own rule is the same three cases (`IntNat.java:126-146`: a literal must be equal, a symbol is bound, anything else fails), which is what the plan ports (`explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:348-356`).
- **A static argument for a static parameter.** The kind-correct helper `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` (`STypesUtil.scala:333-345`) and its list form are called at 17 sites (`git grep` over `ProjectFortress/src`, 19 lines less the two definitions). Two sites make a `TypeArg` for every parameter whatever its kind: `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:83` and `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` (`FnNameInfo.java:162-173` before the edit). They are the Scala and the Java half of the same defect (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:548-580`), and both now call the helper. A third, `STypesUtil.staticParamToArgEnhanced` (`:347-362`), is kind-correct already.
- **The shadow.** `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch` built the same design in seven classpath shadows and measured it; `java/java-shadow.patch` the Java site; `size-probes/keep-size-params.patch` the four lines. They are evidence; section 5 lists where this edit differs.

## 4. The specification

- **Sizes are part of the language.** "Static parameters may include one or more `nat` and `int` parameters ... These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values. A `nat` parameter may be used to instantiate other `nat` parameters, or to appear in any context that a variable of type ℕ32 can appear" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90`). The chapter opens with the 2012 draft's note "Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported" (`:15-17`); the note records the implementation of its day and is what this rung changes for the checker.
- **Inference is assumed, not specified.** "We assume throughout this chapter that all static variables in functional calls have been instantiated or inferred" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`); the inference chapter is a placeholder, "This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). So how an unknown size is treated is not the specification's; it is Pavol's rule of 09-21 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`), an unknown size an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value.
- **Arithmetic in a size is in the language.** "Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as static arguments" (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:23-24`, under the draft's note "Static expressions are not yet supported", `:15`). Refusing it is a limit of the minimal design that the specification does not share; its test is an expected failure (section 6).
- **`bool` parameters are in the language** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:98-115`), and `dim` and `unit` (`:118-135`). Refusing their inference is a limit; its test is an expected failure.
- **The return-type rule.** "Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical (up to α-equivalence) ... Therefore, static parameters ... are ignored in the remainder of this chapter" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`), and the Subtype Rule requires the more specific declaration's return type to be a subtype of the other's (`:158-170`); the same sentence in the basic chapter is `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:33`). The designers' checker implements the rule of their paper instead: `arrow(d1)` must be a subtype of `∀[Δ1, Δ2](S1 ∩ S2) → T2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`), where each declaration's static parameters are its own. Section 5, decision 2, and section 9 say where the two readings part for sizes and for types.

## 5. Decisions, and the deviations from the shadow

**Decision 1: the unsolved size is a node, `_InferenceVarInt(Object id)`, not a reserved name.** Pavol left this to the rung (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`). The alternative is the shadow's `IntRef` named `$nat$k` (option B, `explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:408-428`).
- For the node: it is the codebase's shape for both its inference variables (section 3), and it removes the four costs the shadow names (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:122-126`, `:649-655`, `:695-700`): the size cliques now go through the tree's own `makeSub`, which splits variables from terms by class (`Formula.scala:646`), instead of a hand-written twin; the constraint map is keyed by the node, not by a string; identity is `new Object()`, not a global counter that is not thread-safe; and no program name can collide with it. The node implements `OutAfterTypeChecking`, like `_InferenceVarType`, so one that survives checking is caught by the tree's own assertion (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:263-265`, `STypesUtil.scala:1938-1948`) instead of reaching code generation as a symbol.
- Against: the regeneration. Measured: 26 generated files change and 4 are new (`_InferenceVarInt.java`, `TemplateGap_`, `_Ellipses_`, `_SyntaxTransformation_`), 676 inserted lines, no deletion, plus 8 lines in `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`; `Library/FortressAst.fsi` and `.fss`, which the same generator writes, are unchanged (the generator leaves out `_`-prefixed nodes). That is the record's bound (30 files, `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:69`). The regeneration is deterministic: the hash of the node diff and the four new files was the same after a second regeneration from a touched `Fortress.ast` (`dcd3bcdb…` both times). No other file changed.

**Decision 2: a size the return-type rule leaves free stays bound, as the less specific declaration's own parameter.** Pavol's rule settles that a free size is no error; the implementation was the rung's (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:79`). Three candidates, measured on four probe pairs and their type-parameter twins (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/b1-typecheck-probes.txt`, build 1; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`, the landed edit):

| pair (`probes/`) | the specification | types, the tree (`…T.fss`) | `keep-size-params` alone (build 1) | landed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SubOvUniv`: `Dn.sub[\b,s,o\]: Dn[\T,b,s\]` over `Up.sub: Up[\T,b,s\]`, the library's `subarray` | valid | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `SubOvOneSize`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,3,s\]` | refused | refused (`SubOvOneT`) | **accepted** | refused |
| `SubOvSwap`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,s,b\]` | refused | accepted (`SubOvSwapT`) | accepted | accepted |

- With `keep-size-params.patch` alone the free size is an inference variable that leaks into the arrow checked against (`OverloadingOracle.scala:102-106`), where the second inference solves it: the existential reading. It accepts `SubOvOneSize`, a pair the types' rule refuses and the specification refuses: a stop by the batch record (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:77`), so not taken.
- The shadow's two-line relaxation in `Formula.imp` reads any residue made only of sizes as satisfied, everywhere the checker asks `lteq`, "a pair whose return types agree for one size only" included (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:89-93`); it is the same acceptance, made global. Not taken, and not needed: `keep-size-params.patch` alone already clears the `subarray` refusal the relaxation was written for (`SubOvUniv` above; without it `XXXNatOverrideChecker` gets exactly that error, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/xxx-goes-red-no-keep.txt:30-37`).
- Taken: `satisfiesReturnTypeRule` keeps each size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved as that declaration's own static parameter in the arrow it builds (`OverloadingOracle.scala:90-106`), bound as the paper's `σ∧` binds `Δ2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`). Sizes then read exactly as the tree reads type parameters, the third column. Cost: 12 lines, only when a size escaped (the arrow is untouched otherwise, `:95-97`). `SubOvSwap` stays accepted, as its type twin is today; section 9 says why that is recorded and not stopped on.

**Decision 3: a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is an error at the call** ("Could not infer static argument nat m without context.", `Functionals.scala:247-249`, `ApplicationError.scala:114`). The shadow built only the type half of Pavol's rule (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:649-655`). On the compiled path every static argument of a call names the instantiation the code generator emits (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:36-38`), so a size unsolved there reaches a name. The alternatives were to leave the variable in the static arguments for the run-time rung, which would reach `NamingCzar` as an unknown node or trip the tree's `OutAfterTypeChecking` assertion as an internal bug, both in files that are not this rung's; or to default it to `0`, which is E1, not taken by Pavol. The consequence goes to Pavol: a compiled call to a function with a dead size is refused (`probes/DeadSize.fss`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`), where `walk` binds it to `Bottom` and runs (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt`); the library's six vector `DOT` declarations with a dead `nat m, nat p` (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:153-160`) are such functions, so E3, deleting them, is what makes their compiled calls check. The declarations themselves pass, as the rule says.

**Decision 4: `solve` returns a triple** (the size substitution third) and its one test line changes (`FormulaJUTest.scala:177`); `And` and `Conjuncts` take the size map as a defaulted third field. The shadow kept `solve` a pair beside a new `solveN` and added two-argument companions, because its classpath shadow had to link against classes compiled for the tree (`shadow.patch`, "keeps the old shape"); a real edit has no such constraint.

**Decision 5: the test shapes.** The brief's `.test` files stop at `compile`. Two programs cannot: code generation refuses a sized overload set (`OverloadSet.java:1199`, "Only handling some static args of generic types") and a size in an `extends` clause (`CodeGen.java:5793`, "Only emitting RTTI for types right now"), both the run-time rung's. Each is one `XXX` test driving `compile` with `compile_exception_contains`, the shape of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXObjExprRungS.test:1-3`: it is green only if the checker accepts the program (a checker refusal is not the exception) and code generation then refuses it, so it gates this rung's acceptance and the run-time rung's defect at once. A plain `typecheck` test beside it over the same component was tried and dropped: the harness shuffles `.test` files with a clock seed (`FileTests.java:1116`, `:1135-1137`), and after a `typecheck` of an unchanged component a `compile` writes nothing and exits 0 (measured: `fortress compile` of `XXXNatDispArmChecker.fss` after its typecheck printed nothing, exit 0), so the pair's verdict would depend on the order.

**Deviations from the shadow, one line each.**
- The inference variable is a node (decision 1), not `$nat$k`.
- `solve` is a triple (decision 4); no `solveN`, no two-argument companions.
- The return-type rule: bound escaped sizes (decision 2), not the `Formula.imp` relaxation.
- `keep-size-params.patch` is in as a plain edit (`TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:484-488`), without its probe switch.
- The name half of Pavol's rule is in (decision 3); the shadow had only the type half.
- Arithmetic is refused on the static argument as well as the type (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:144-145`), the gap the shadow named (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:213-220`): `unbox[\3\](Box[\2 + 1\](7))` now gets "Ill-formed static argument: 2+1" as well as "not applicable" (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/compile-probes.txt`). The message says "not supported by the type checker" where the shadow's said "is not checked".
- `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` calls `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` instead of building `IntArg(IntRef)` by hand (`java/java-shadow.patch`).
- `pEqv` on two size variables is `and(...)` as in the op precedent (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:345`), where the shadow used `pAnd`; the two agree under negation.
- `imp`'s size conjunct runs in the type track's direction (`Formula.scala:205`); the op track's conjunct runs the other way (`:204`), a difference read and not measured, left as it is.
- Not taken from `shadow.patch`: the three probe switches, the zero probe's `checkP` and `TypeHierarchyChecker` switches, the `parents`/`excludesClause` memo (the tree landed its own, `d28cf74d0`), and the variance branch in `pSub`'s trait case (a size parameter has no variance in the grammar, `trait-parameters.tex:71-74`).

**Deviations from the specification's spelling.** Arithmetic in a size is refused (section 4); `bool`, `dim` and `unit` inference is refused; a dead size at a call is refused (decision 3, Pavol's rule where the specification is silent); `SubOvSwap` is accepted, as for types (section 9).

## 4. The specification

- **Sizes are part of the language.** "Static parameters may include one or more `nat` and `int` parameters ... These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values. A `nat` parameter may be used to instantiate other `nat` parameters, or to appear in any context that a variable of type ℕ32 can appear" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90`). The chapter opens with the 2012 draft's note "Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported" (`:15-17`); the note records the implementation of its day and is what this rung changes for the checker.
- **Inference is assumed, not specified.** "We assume throughout this chapter that all static variables in functional calls have been instantiated or inferred" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`); the inference chapter is a placeholder, "This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). So how an unknown size is treated is not the specification's; it is Pavol's rule of 09-21 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`), an unknown size an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value.
- **Arithmetic in a size is in the language.** "Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as static arguments" (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:23-24`, under the draft's note "Static expressions are not yet supported", `:15`). Refusing it is a limit of the minimal design that the specification does not share; its test is an expected failure (section 6).
- **`bool` parameters are in the language** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:98-115`), and `dim` and `unit` (`:118-135`). Refusing their inference is a limit; its test is an expected failure.
- **The return-type rule.** "Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical (up to α-equivalence) ... Therefore, static parameters ... are ignored in the remainder of this chapter" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`), and the Subtype Rule requires the more specific declaration's return type to be a subtype of the other's (`:158-170`); the same sentence in the basic chapter is `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:33`). The designers' checker implements the rule of their paper instead: `arrow(d1)` must be a subtype of `∀[Δ1, Δ2](S1 ∩ S2) → T2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`), where each declaration's static parameters are its own. Section 5, decision 2, and section 9 say where the two readings part for sizes and for types.

Walk's answer against the compiled checker's verdict for programs with a size; walk against the compiled run for the one without (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-tests.txt`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/compile-probes.txt`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`).

**Why `SubOvSwap` is recorded and not a stop.** The stop is a reading of a size that accepts what the specification refuses (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:77`). This acceptance is not a reading of sizes: the tree accepts the same shape with type parameters (`SubOvSwapT`) and the compiled run then fails (`SubOvSwapTRun`). It comes from the checker's rule letting the more specific declaration choose its own instantiation (`TypeSchemaAnalyzer.subUA`, `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:130-141`, the paper's `arrow(d1) ≤ σ∧`), where the specification identifies the two declarations' static parameters (`advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`). Making sizes stricter than types here would enforce that sentence for sizes only, which the rung must not do (`CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:77`, "this rung neither enforces it nor relaxes it further"). - **The per-declaration run.** PERDECL

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What each top-level declaration of the interpreter's library becomes, before
and after the nat shadow.
Input: two PhaseProbe -Dprobe.tolerant=true runs (see run-all.sh step 3b), which
print one @@TC DECL-OK / @@TC DECL-CRASH line per top-level declaration of the
component.  Output: the counts, the fate of every declaration that changed, and
the crash sites that remain.
"""
import sys, collections
def read(path):
    decls = {}                      # span -> (kind, fate, detail)
    order = []
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        if line.startswith("@@TC DECL-OK\t"):
            _, kind, span, errs = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 3)
            decls[span] = (kind, "ok", errs)
            order.append(span)
        elif line.startswith("@@TC DECL-CRASH\t"):
            f = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            kind, span, exc, site, msg = f[1], f[2], f[3], f[4], (f[5] if len(f) > 5 else "")
# Per top-level declaration of Library/FortressLibrary.fss, the checker's fate

## Where the work stands

The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the latest committed specification (`Specification/`, the July 2012 draft), not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).

The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). Between that library and bytecode stands the checker, not desugaring or code generation; it reports 103 errors on the library, the count since climb batch 3, and a batch's count may only fall from it or declare its rise (`coordinator/FACTS.md` § The checker and the one library). The route on the checker's multiple instantiation exclusion, the rul

Decided, in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`: the goal and its measuring stick (2026-09-16); test first, the test written and seen failing before the fix and kept in the corpus from then on (2026-09-17); the workflow, with workers pushing to their own `wip/` branches, the script in the repository and the higher tier called only at a refusal, a stop or a red gate (2026-09-18), narrowed to a judge's second ruling on the same rung or tree (2026-09-24); unboxed `double[]` storage and the `nat` sizes taken together, as the team designed them (2026-09-19); the tier rule, workers on the cheaper tier and a 

What comes next, in the order the boot note gives (`coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-19/held-list.md`, under "Boot note to the resumed coordinator", which is kept current at every compaction): batch 4's manifest for his go, three rungs that share no file: the interpreter coercion rung (A's first), a specification rung that revises the sentences the decision changes and points at a decision record preserving the original text, the reasoning and route C, and the size wall's first rung, launched after the weekly usage reset; the one workflow option not yet put to him (approvals with required correc

## 2. Where the fix belongs

The map's row for `nat` and `int` parameters puts the wall in the checker: `STypesUtil.scala:550-557`, "interp works / comp absent — the wall is the checker, not codegen" (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:233`; `:355` in the path table). The checker is the TYPECHECK phase, `compiler/StaticChecker.java` calling the Scala checker (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:266`, `:353`). Code generation already names a size (`NamingCzar.forIntRef`/`forIntBase`, `explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:36-38`) and a sized program then fails at load, which is the run-time rung's (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:93`). So the fix is in `scala_src/`, and in the one Java class the checker calls on every method invocation, `FnNameInfo.boundsFor`, reached from `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:606` and `:730`. Nothing in `compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `runtimeSystem/`, `compiler/runtimeValues/`, `CodeGen.java`, `OverloadSet.java`, `Library/` or `interpreter/` was edited.

## 3. Precedent search

- **Inference variables.** The checker has two, both syntax-tree nodes minted with `new Object()` identity: `_InferenceVarType` (`Fortress.ast:1061`, `NodeFactory.java:1166-1175`) and `_InferenceVarOp` (`Fortress.ast:1593`, `NodeFactory.java:1178-1180`). No inference variable in the tree is a reserved name. The size variable follows them (decision 1).
- **Equality-only constraints.** The operator track is the one whose constraints are equalities (`OPrimitive(pe, ne)`, `Formula.scala:57-61`): its reduce steps `oSimplify`, `oContradiction`, `oTrivial` (`:355-371`), its cliques through `getCliques` and `makeSub` (`:640-642`), its primitive constructors (`:799-806`) and `TypeAnalyzer.pEqv(Op, Op)` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:342-348`). The size track copies each of these once, with `nEq` in place of `==`. The interpreter's rule is the same three cases (`IntNat.java:126-146`: a literal must be equal, a symbol is bound, anything else fails), which is what the plan ports (`explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:348-356`).
- **A static argument for a static parameter.** The kind-correct `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` (`STypesUtil.scala:333-345`) and its list form are called at 17 sites (`grep` of `staticParamsToArgs\|staticParamToArg` over `ProjectFortress/src`, 19 lines less the two definitions). Two sites made a `TypeArg` for every parameter whatever its kind: `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:83` and `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` (`FnNameInfo.java:162-173` before the edit), the Scala and the Java half of one defect (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:548-580`); both now call the helper. A third helper, `staticParamToArgEnhanced` (`:347-362`), is kind-correct already.
- **The shadow.** `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch` built this design in classpath shadows and measured it; `java/java-shadow.patch` the Java site; `size-probes/keep-size-params.patch` the four lines. They are evidence; section 5 lists where the edit differs.

## 4. The specification

- **Sizes are part of the language.** "Static parameters may include one or more `nat` and `int` parameters ... These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values. A `nat` parameter may be used to instantiate other `nat` parameters, or to appear in any context that a variable of type ℕ32 can appear" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90`). The chapter opens with the 2012 draft's note "Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported" (`:15-17`), which records the implementation of its day.
- **Inference is assumed, not specified.** "We assume throughout this chapter that all static variables in functional calls have been instantiated or inferred" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`); the inference chapter is a placeholder, "This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). How an unknown size is treated is therefore Pavol's rule of 09-21 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`): an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value.
- **Arithmetic in a size is in the language.** "Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as static arguments" (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:23-24`, under the draft note "Static expressions are not yet supported", `:15`). Refusing it is a limit of the minimal design that the specification does not share; its test is an expected failure (section 6).
- **`bool`, `dim` and `unit` parameters are in the language** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:98-115`, `:118-135`). Refusing their inference is a limit; its test is an expected failure.
- **The return-type rule.** "Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical (up to α-equivalence) ... Therefore, static parameters ... are ignored in the remainder of this chapter" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`), and the Subtype Rule requires the more specific declaration's return type to be a subtype of the other's (`:158-170`); the same sentence in the basic chapter is `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:33`). The designers' checker implements the rule of their paper instead: `arrow(d1)` must be a subtype of `∀[Δ1, Δ2](S1 ∩ S2) → T2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`), each declaration's static parameters its own. Section 5, decision 2, and section 9 say where the two readings part.

## 5. Decisions, and the deviations from the shadow

**Decision 1: the unknown size is a node, `_InferenceVarInt(Object id)`, not a reserved name.** Pavol left this to the rung (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`). The alternative is the shadow's `IntRef` named `$nat$k` (option B, `explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:408-428`).
- For the node: it is the codebase's shape for both its inference variables (section 3), and it removes the four costs the shadow names (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:122-126`, `:649-655`, `:695-700`): the size cliques go through the tree's own `makeSub`, which splits variables from terms by class (`Formula.scala:646`), instead of a hand-written twin; the constraint map is keyed by the node, not by a string; identity is `new Object()`, not a global counter that is not thread-safe; and no program name can collide with it. The node implements `OutAfterTypeChecking`, like `_InferenceVarType`, so one that survives checking trips the tree's own assertion (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:263-265`, `STypesUtil.scala:1938-1948`) instead of reaching code generation as a symbol.
- Against: the regeneration. Measured: 26 generated files change and 4 are new (`_InferenceVarInt.java`, `TemplateGap_InferenceVarInt.java`, `_Ellipses_InferenceVarInt.java`, `_SyntaxTransformation_InferenceVarInt.java`), 676 inserted lines and no deletion, plus 8 lines in `scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala`; `Library/FortressAst.fsi` and `.fss`, which the same target writes, are unchanged (the generator leaves `_`-prefixed nodes out of them). That is the record's bound of about 30 files (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:69`). The regeneration is deterministic: the SHA-256 of the node diff with the four new files was `dcd3bcdb…` after the first regeneration and again after a second one from a touched `Fortress.ast`; no other file changed.

**Decision 2: a size the return-type rule leaves free stays bound, as the less specific declaration's own parameter.** Pavol's rule settles that a free size is no error; the implementation was the rung's (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:79`). Measured on three probe pairs and their type-parameter twins (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/b1-typecheck-probes.txt`, build 1, `keep-size-params` without this decision; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`, the landed edit):

| pair (`probes/`) | the specification | types in the tree (`…T.fss`) | `keep-size-params` alone (build 1) | landed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SubOvUniv`: `Dn.sub[\b,s,o\]: Dn[\T,b,s\]` over `Up.sub: Up[\T,b,s\]`, the library's `subarray` | valid | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `SubOvOneSize`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,3,s\]` | refused | refused (`SubOvOneT`) | **accepted** | refused |
| `SubOvSwap`: `Dn.sub` returns `Dn[\T,s,b\]` | refused | accepted (`SubOvSwapT`) | accepted | accepted |

- With `keep-size-params.patch` alone the free size is an inference variable that leaks into the arrow checked against (`OverloadingOracle.scala:102-106`), where the second inference solves it: the existential reading. It accepts `SubOvOneSize`, which the types' rule refuses and the specification refuses. That is the stop of the batch record (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:77`), so it was not kept.
- The shadow's two-line relaxation in `Formula.imp` reads any residue made only of sizes as satisfied, everywhere the checker asks `lteq`, "a pair whose return types agree for one size only" included (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:89-93`): the same acceptance made global. Not taken, and not needed: `keep-size-params.patch` alone already clears the `subarray` refusal the relaxation was written for (the first row above; with `keep-size-params` off, `XXXNatOverrideChecker` gets exactly that error, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/xxx-goes-red-no-keep.txt:23-33`).

Sizes then read exactly as the tree reads type parameters, the third column. Cost: 12 lines, active only when a size escaped (the arrow is untouched otherwise, `:95-97`). `SubOvSwap` stays accepted, as its type twin is today; section 9 says why that is recorded and not stopped on.

**Decision 3: a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is an error at the call** ("Could not infer static argument nat m without context.", `Functionals.scala:247-249`, `ApplicationError.scala:114`). The shadow built only the type half of Pavol's rule (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:649-655`). On the compiled path every static argument of a call names the instantiation the code generator emits (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/java.md:36-38`), so a size unsolved there reaches a name. The alternatives were to leave the variable in the static arguments for the run-time rung, where it would reach `NamingCzar` as an unknown node or trip the `OutAfterTypeChecking` assertion as an internal bug, both in files that are not this rung's; or to default it to `0`, decision E1, which Pavol did not take. The consequence goes to Pavol: a compiled call to a function with a dead size is refused (`probes/DeadSize.fss`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt:26-33`), where `walk` binds it to `Bottom` and runs (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt:35-40`). The library's six vector `DOT` declarations with a dead `nat m, nat p` (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:153-160`) are such functions, so E3, deleting those parameters, is what lets their compiled calls check. The declarations themselves pass, as the rule says.

**Decision 4: `solve` returns a triple**, the size substitution third, and its one test line changes (`FormulaJUTest.scala:177`); `And` and `Conjuncts` take the size map as a defaulted third field. The shadow kept `solve` a pair beside a new `solveN` and added two-argument companions because its classpath shadow had to link against classes compiled for the tree; a real edit has no such constraint.

**Decision 5: the test shapes.** The brief's `.test` files stop at `compile`. Two programs cannot pass `compile`: code generation refuses a sized overload set (`OverloadSet.java:1199`, "Only handling some static args of generic types") and a size in an `extends` clause (`CodeGen.java:5793`, "Only emitting RTTI for types right now"), both the run-time rung's. Each is one `XXX` test driving `compile` with `compile_exception_contains`, the shape of `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXObjExprRungS.test:1-3`: it is green only if the checker accepts the program (a checker refusal is not that exception) and code generation then refuses it, so it gates this rung's acceptance and the run-time rung's defect at once. A plain `typecheck` test over the same component was tried and dropped: the harness orders `.test` files by a clock-seeded shuffle (`FileTests.java:1116`, `:1135-1137`), and after a `typecheck` of an unchanged component a `compile` writes nothing and exits 0 (measured by hand: `fortress compile compiler_tests/XXXNatDispArmChecker.fss` after its typecheck printed nothing, exit 0), so the pair's verdict would depend on the order.

**Deviations from the shadow, one line each.**
- The inference variable is a node (decision 1), not `$nat$k`.
- `solve` is a triple (decision 4); no `solveN`, no two-argument companions.
- The return-type rule binds escaped sizes (decision 2); no `Formula.imp` relaxation.
- `keep-size-params.patch` is a plain edit (`TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:484-488`), without its probe switch.
- The name half of Pavol's rule is in (decision 3); the shadow had only the type half.
- Arithmetic is refused on the static argument as well as on the type (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:144-145`), the gap the shadow named (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md:213-220`): `unbox[\3\](Box[\2 + 1\](7))` now also gets "Ill-formed static argument: 2+1" (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/compile-probes.txt:2-10`). The message says "is not supported by the type checker" where the shadow's said "is not checked".
- `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` calls `STypesUtil.staticParamToArg` instead of building `IntArg(IntRef)` by hand (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/java/java-shadow.patch`).
- `pEqv` on two size variables is `and(...)` as the op precedent writes it (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:345`, `:356`), where the shadow used `pAnd`; the two agree under negation.
- `imp`'s size conjunct runs in the type track's direction (`Formula.scala:203-205`); the op track's conjunct runs the other way (`:204`), a difference read and not measured, left as it is.
- Not taken from `shadow.patch`: its three probe switches, the zero probe's `checkP` and `TypeHierarchyChecker` switches, the `parents`/`excludesClause` memo (the tree landed its own, `d28cf74d0`), and the variance branch in `pSub`'s trait case (a size parameter has no variance in the grammar, `trait-parameters.tex:71-74`).

## 4. The specification

- **Sizes are part of the language.** "Static parameters may include one or more `nat` and `int` parameters ... These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values. A `nat` parameter may be used to instantiate other `nat` parameters, or to appear in any context that a variable of type ℕ32 can appear" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:68-90`). The chapter opens with the 2012 draft's note "Non-type static parameters and static expressions are not yet supported" (`:15-17`), which records the implementation of its day.
- **Inference is assumed, not specified.** "We assume throughout this chapter that all static variables in functional calls have been instantiated or inferred" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`); the inference chapter is a placeholder, "This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism" (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). How an unknown size is treated is therefore Pavol's rule of 09-21 (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`): an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value.
- **Arithmetic in a size is in the language.** "Static expressions which use a restricted subset of operations can occur as static arguments" (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:23-24`, under the draft note "Static expressions are not yet supported", `:15`). Refusing it is a limit of the minimal design that the specification does not share; its test is an expected failure (section 6).
- **`bool`, `dim` and `unit` parameters are in the language** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:98-115`, `:118-135`). Refusing their inference is a limit; its test is an expected failure.
- **The return-type rule.** "Overloaded declarations must have static parameters that are identical (up to α-equivalence) ... Therefore, static parameters ... are ignored in the remainder of this chapter" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`), and the Subtype Rule requires the more specific declaration's return type to be a subtype of the other's (`:158-170`); the same sentence in the basic chapter is `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:33`). The designers' checker implements the rule of their paper instead: `arrow(d1)` must be a subtype of `∀[Δ1, Δ2](S1 ∩ S2) → T2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`), each declaration's static parameters its own. Section 5, decision 2, and section 9 say where the two readings part.

## FACTS.md

- **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters** (2026-09-26, climb batch 4 rung N; `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md`). A size is a symbol or a literal compared by equality; an unknown one is an inference variable of its own, a new syntax-tree node `_InferenceVarInt` beside the two the checker had (30 regenerated node files, 26 changed and 4 new, deterministic), with a third constraint track in `Formula`; `keep-size-params` in `TypeSchemaAnalyzer`; kind-correct static arguments in `AbstractMethodChecker` and `FnNameInfo.boundsFor`; arithmetic in a size, and inference of a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` parameter, refused by name; a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is "Could not infer static argument ... without context". Inferred, written-out, method-on-sized-receiver and several-sizes-at-one-call programs check (`compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`); a mismatch is refused (`XXXNatMismatchChecker`). What stays for the run-time rung: a sized program fails at load (`3$RTTIc`, `XXXNatArgRungS`), and code generation refuses a sized overload set (`OverloadSet.java:1199`, `XXXNatDispArmChecker`) and a size in `extends` (`CodeGen.java:5793`, `XXXNatOverrideChecker`). The checker count over the interpreter's library goes 103 → 125 with the crash row `none`: 22 `Invalid overloading of fill` errors in `NativeArray` that the crash hid, nothing reported before gone. Per top-level declaration of `FortressLibrary.fss`: 237 clean / 97 with errors / 112 crashes → 286 / 155 / 5, the five crashes the untyped-local-parameter and `Character` sites the shadow left (`compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/perdecl-fates.txt`).
- **The return-type rule now reads a size as it reads a type parameter** (2026-09-26, rung N). With `keep-size-params` alone a size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved leaked into the checked arrow as an inference variable and was solved there, accepting an override that returns `Dn[\T,3,s\]` over `Up[\T,b,s\]`, which the type-parameter twin refuses; `OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule` now keeps such a size as that declaration's own parameter, bound as the paper's `σ∧` binds `Δ2` (`Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`). The shadow's `Formula.imp` relaxation was not needed: `keep-size-params` alone clears the `subarray` refusal (`compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt`, `b1-typecheck-probes.txt`, `xxx-goes-red-no-keep.txt`).
- **The checker's return-type rule lets the more specific declaration choose its own instantiation, so an override that permutes its own static parameters in its return type type-checks and fails at run time** (2026-09-26, rung N; row 387). `SubOvSwapTRun` (type parameters, no size) compiles and dies with `ClassCastException`; `walk` refuses the binding; sizes read the same after rung N. The specification refuses the pair (`advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`, `:158-170`); the repair is reading the two declarations' static parameters as shared, the sentence of `basic/overloading.tex:100-107` that is Pavol's open decision (`compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/compile-probes.txt:29-33`, `walk-probes.txt:50-69`).

## Gap ledger

**Note to append to row 307** (rows are never renumbered or moved): "Fixed for the checker in climb batch 4 rung N (commit at the gather), 2026-09-26: the three spellings of this row now pass the compiled checker (`compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`), sizes compared as symbols and literals by `Formula`'s third track with an `_InferenceVarInt` node, arithmetic in a size and `bool`/`dim`/`unit` inference refused by name (`XXXNatArithChecker`, `XXXNatBoolChecker`), the checker count 103 → 125 with no crash (`compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/checker-count-after.txt`). - claim: **the compiled checker's return-type rule accepts an override whose return type permutes its own static parameters, and the program then fails at run time**: `Dn.sub[\U, V\](m: ZZ32): Dn[\V, U\]` beside `Up.sub[\U, V\](m: ZZ32): Up[\U, V\]`, with `Dn[\U0, V0\] extends Up[\U0, V0\]`, type-checks; compiled, `u.sub[\Boolean, ZZ64\](3)` on a `Dn` held as `Up[\ZZ32, String\]` returns a `Dn[\ZZ64, Boolean\]` and the run dies with `ClassCastException: ... Dn?...FZZ64,...FBoolean? cannot be cast to ... Up?...FBoolean,...FZZ64?`; `walk` refuses the binding (`RHS expression type Dn[\ZZ64,Boolean\] is not assignable to LHS type Up[\Boolean,ZZ64\]`). The same with sizes after climb batch 4 rung N (`SubOvSwap`, `SubOvSwapRun`: the checker accepts, `walk` refuses `Dn[\5,2\]` as `Up[\2,5\]`).
- status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED
- class: checker defect against the specification, pre-existing for type parameters
- spec citation: `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103` (static parameters identical up to α-equivalence, then ignored) and `:158-170` (the Subtype Rule's return types); `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`; the checker follows the designers' paper instead, `Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick:166-172`
- reproducer: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/SubOvSwapTRun.fss`, `SubOvSwapT.fss`, `SubOvSwap.fss`, `SubOvSwapRun.fss`; captures `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/compile-probes.txt:29-33`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/typecheck-probes.txt:12-13`, `:24-25`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt:50-69`
- found by: climb batch 4 rung N, 2026-09-26
- notes / workaround: the fix is in the return-type check, `OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/overloading/OverloadingOracle.scala:81-117`), which ends in `subtypeUA(fa, ra)`, whose branch "s has static parameters and t does not" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:132-141`) re-infers the more specific declaration's instantiation; reading the two declarations' parameters as shared, as the specification does, means comparing the return types with those parameters identified by position, which is the static-parameter sentence of `basic/overloading.tex:100-107`, Pavol's open decision. Not expressible as an expected-failure test: an `XXX` test demands a failing command, and here the command succeeds.

**New row 388 (provisional).**
- claim: **`walk` cannot infer a generic method's own static argument, of a type or a size, nor a `bool` static argument of a function**: `Plain(7).idxT(BoxT[\ZZ32\](5))` with `idxT[\U\](b: BoxT[\U\])` fails `Unification error: Closure/Constructor for idxT param 1 (b:BoxT[\U@…\]) got arg BoxT[\ZZ32\]`, on a plain and on a generic receiver, and the size twin `idx[\nat j\](b: Box[\j\])` the same; the same declarations as top-level functions are inferred (5, 5); written out, all run. `unflag(Flag[\true\](7))` with `unflag[\bool b\](f: Flag[\b\])` fails `Cannot unify Flag[\true\] ... with Flag[\b\]`; `unflag[\true\](…)` prints 7. The compiled checker infers the method cases and refuses the `bool` one by name.
- status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED
- class: interpreter gap
- spec citation: silent: `Specification/basic/inference.tex:15` is a placeholder and `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138` assumes static arguments "instantiated or inferred"; `bool` parameters `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:101-120`
- reproducer: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/MethInferT.fss`, `MethInferPlain.fss`, `FnInferNatVsType.fss`, `BoolWritten.fss`; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-probes.txt:2-17`, `:70-78`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NatMethodChecker.fss` and `XXXNatBoolChecker.fss` under `walk`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/walk-tests.txt:8-16`, `:42-52`
- found by: climb batch 4 rung N, 2026-09-26
- notes / workaround: the specification is silent, so the behaviour is a choice: the interpreter infers a function's static arguments of both kinds and the compiled checker infers a method's, so the method case is a gap in one path, not a rule of the language; write the static arguments at the call. The home is a probe and this row, not an expected-failure test, because the prose does not settle it.

**New row 389 (provisional).**
- claim: **six declarations of `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` that the checker passed clean each gain one error once it reaches sizes** (per top-level declaration, `PhaseProbe`, the interpreter's library): `__builtinFactory2` (`:2597-2602`), whose `then` branch is `Array2[\T,0,s0,0,s1\]` where the declared type is `Array2[\T,b0,s0,b1,s1\]`, sound only by its run-time guard `b0=0 AND b1=0`; `array2(f)` (`:2611-2612`), whose `.fill(f)` resolves to the general `fill` of the overload set the checker count's 22 new errors refuse; and `BIG LEXICO`, `BIG SQCUP`, `BIG MINNUM`, `BIG MAXNUM` (`:129-130`, `:1446-1447`, `:3153-3154`, `:3160-3161`), each `opr BIG X(g) = __bigOperatorSugar[…](BIG X(), g)` with no return type in the component, to which the checker gives the api's nullary overload's return type ("Function body has type TotalComparison, but declared return type is BigReduction[\TotalComparison,TotalComparison\]").
- status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED for the six errors; the mechanism of the last four not isolated
- class: library defect (`__builtinFactory2`; the four omit a return type), and a checker question (the choice of the nullary overload's return type)
- spec citation: the typing of `if` against a declared return type (`__builtinFactory2`); `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:17`, a draft note, "Return types are required for overloaded functional declarations" (the four)
- reproducer: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/perdecl-fates.txt:29`, `:41`, `:88`, `:89`, `:110`, `:111`; error texts `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/perdecl-after.txt:1642`, `:1643`, `:1670`, `:1671`, `:1828`, `:1920`; the A/B with two `IntArg`s always equal and `keep-size-params` off, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/perdecl-ab-fates.txt:106-107` (only `MINNUM` and `MAXNUM` keep their error)
- found by: the nat shadow (five of them, `explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:80-87`); measured on the tree by climb batch 4 rung N, 2026-09-26
- notes / workaround: the four `BIG` declarations take the api's return types in the component (`: TotalComparison`, `: UniqueItem[\T\]`, `: RR64`), four library tokens; `__builtinFactory2` needs its two branches typed apart, since no static rule reads the guard; `array2(f)` goes with the `fill` family (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:41`). None of the six is in the gate's count, which does not reach the component's declarations.

## Handover state line

Climb batch 4 rung N (`rung-nat-checker`): the compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters by the minimal design (symbols and literals, equality, no arithmetic), with an `_InferenceVarInt` node, `keep-size-params`, and a return-type rule that reads a size as a type parameter; the checker count is 125 with no crash (22 `fill` overloading errors in `NativeArray` that the crash hid), row 307 closes for the checker, and a sized program still fails at load and at code generation, gated for the run-time rung.

## What comes back to Pavol

- The two choices and why: the unknown size is a node, not a reserved name (the codebase's shape for both its inference variables; 30 generated files, deterministic); a size the return-type rule leaves free stays the less specific declaration's own parameter, so sizes read as type parameters do (the leaked-variable reading accepted an override the types' rule refuses; the shadow's relaxation was not needed).
- A third, taken by the rung inside your rule of 09-21: a size left unknown in a call's static arguments is an error, because on the compiled path those arguments name the instantiation. So a compiled call to a function with a dead size is refused where `walk` runs it (`probes/DeadSize.fss`); the library's six vector `DOT` declarations with a dead `nat m, nat p` are such functions, which makes E3 the step that lets their compiled calls check.
- The checker count, 125 with `none`, and the `NativeArray` errors now visible: 22 `Invalid overloading of fill`.
- The per-declaration findings: 112 crashes → 5 (none about sizes); six declarations gain one error each (row 389), one of them, `__builtinFactory2`, a true positive.
- Row 387: the return-type rule accepts an override that permutes its own static parameters and the compiled run then fails, for type parameters today; its repair is the static-parameter sentence, your open decision.
EOF_RECORD
